pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Irregularly shaped polygonal and sub-rounded dark regions with moderate edge gradients. The patches are larger and more densely packed on the upper dorsal area, transitioning to smaller, more discrete shapes on the posterior flank.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of light-colored interstitial pathways forming a topological web. Junction nodes predominantly feature three-way intersections. Pixel thickness is variable, thinning significantly around the areas of textural disruption.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: High-frequency, low-amplitude serrated silhouette of dark hair along the upper neck and shoulder. The mane appears as a dense, fibrous vertical projection against the background.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Extensive clusters of raised, hyper-pigmented, and crusty nodular masses are visible along the upper neck and upper flank, causing significant textural disruption to the underlying pelage.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Widespread presence of raised, warty lesions and grayish-brown nodules concentrated on the shoulders and neck, consistent with significant physical skin trauma or disease-related structural changes.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of multiple small birds (oxpeckers) perched along the mane and upper dorsal ridge, causing localized pixel occlusions of the giraffe's profile.
